key_terms.كِتَابُ اللَّهِ: The Book of God (referring to the Qur'an)

ai.seo_question: What are the metaphors used to describe the Holy Qur'an in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi employs these metaphors to affirm the Qur'an's status as the primary source of divine guidance alongside the Prophet, emphasizing its clarity and permanence. In Shia tradition, this passage underscores the Qur'an's role as a 'speaking' authority that, unlike the silent text, actively guides the faithful through the Imams who interpret its depths. The imagery of an indestructible house and invincible allies highlights the spiritual resilience and eternal nature of divine revelation.
